# Original runtime signature observations

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz), [index](index.json) and
[validation record](validation.json) retain 93 original records. Seven complete
projects have fourteen actual ordinary/selected CLI observations: ordinary
enum/match controls succeed, quantum nominal execution reaches its concrete
profile barriers, and ordinary quantum inspection/hidden observation reach
their actual type/effect errors. The prior CLI and native executables are
hash-bound observations, without current-head build attestation.

The new internal reader retains complete runtime prefixes around quantum
owners, including nested products and ordinary zero-width parameters. It reuses
the original finite-type and import readers; an annotation read is not a checked
body effect. The first reserved `Type` identifier error and separate default-list
projection error remain unchanged. Separate repairs compile with strict package
options; 22 small kernel reductions and a 21,130-declaration audit pass using
only the existing standard axiom basis. Single-process peak memory is about
1.65 GiB. No maximum-size quantum case is generated.

Original observers, source objects, complete diagnostic streams and source/import
maps remain inert data. Passive tests neither extract nor replay them. These
component compiles use stable existing imports and do not establish a full
dependency replay, source-body theorem or native execution gate. Current proof
records require genuine maintenance for this candidate. Ordinary/selected typed
execution, complete body/code/effect binding and generic/static transport remain
unfinished; #64 and #195 remain open.

The archived observer initially reports 23 reductions; enumerating the actual
theorem declarations gives 22. The separate validation record corrects that
count without rewriting the original observer or its archive.

## Mixed runtime root component

The separate [root archive](runtime-root-first.tar.xz),
[root index](runtime-root-index.json) and [root validation](runtime-root-validation.json)
retain 130 records without altering the signature history above. Four desired
programs have eight real prior-CLI observations: six concrete profile barriers
and two actual hidden-discard effect refusals. These are informed integration
inputs, not an independent initial-authoring study or current native attestation.

First storage, missing exact-composition API, annotation-decidability and test
elaboration failures remain alongside separate repairs. The compiled audit's
generated partial-recursion refusal is retained; a bounded Nat recursion and
generic complete-history-length theorem repair it without relaxing the audit.
The corrected component compiles 24 small kernel reductions, evaluates all 21
mixed-root controls and audits 21,637 declarations with only the existing
standard axiom basis. The observed single-process peak is 905,428,992 bytes
(about 0.84 GiB). New cases use at most three physical bits.

The root retains original full type queries, exact ordinary storage, ordered
quantum ports and the same freshly validated Raw graph. Independent canonical
ordinary inputs and every hidden quantum history receive storage/code checks,
including zero-probability results. Lifted exact logical maps must equal their
actual physical maps; their complete Gram sum is checked. A generic theorem
rules out a rectangular logical Unitary label. Public Observe is not sharpened.
This is actual-IR typing and exact-computation evidence, not an arbitrary
algorithm request, complex-denotation or source/runtime preservation theorem.

At that component checkpoint, native/QDV dispatch and normal project/selected
execution did not use it. Generic/static and wider qmatch integration, complete fresh
package replay, genuine proof-record maintenance and hosted CI/review remain
required. #64/#195 stay open; no new guarantee or release is claimed. Historical
observers and sources are never executed or extracted by retention tests.

## Native runtime transport

The separate [transport archive](runtime-transport-first.tar.xz),
[transport index](runtime-transport-index.json) and
[transport validation](runtime-transport-validation.json) retain 572 inert
records. The original incompatible Homebrew compiler observations, Rust closure
type error and audit working-directory error remain alongside their corrections.
No prior source, diagnostic or archive above is replaced.

The current native mode independently reads the full mixed request and compares
the retained Rust graph, type/storage forests and public effect through QDV.
An accepted program and its clones retain those same objects. Fresh rechecking
detects altered metadata and graph views; portable export cannot erase them.
Zero-width source parameters still prevent closed simulation and sampling.
Tests include code-space leakage, hidden observation under a pure label,
invalid ordinary values on zero-probability histories, nominal/axis substitution
and singleton quantum owners. New cases use at most three physical bits.

The current kernel rebuild rehashes original source/dependency traces while
reusing warm artifacts. Its compiled audit checks 21,744 declarations with only
the existing standard axioms. Rust 1.99.1 and MSRV 1.85.0 each pass the ten new
native/codec tests and thirteen existing ordinary-root tests, with zero skips.
Two native-context tests and stable all-target warnings-denied Clippy also pass.
Observed peak memory is 2,784,903,168 bytes (about 2.59 GiB). These checks do not
constitute a fresh replay of every unchanged dependency, current-proof-record
maintenance, source/runtime preservation or an independent algorithm contract.
Normal `.qli` project/selected lowering, generic/static transport, wider qmatch,
full proof maintenance and hosted CI/review remain required. #64/#195 stay open.

## Common source integration

The separate [source archive](runtime-source-first.tar.xz),
[source index](runtime-source-index.json) and
[source validation](runtime-source-validation.json) preserve the original Rust
field/borrow errors, overly broad nominal-type refusal, obsolete regression
expectations and first CLI usage error alongside their separate repairs.
Source objects and observed streams remain inert; no previous history is changed.

Nongeneric project and selected `.qli` interfaces now reach the runtime gate
through the common emitter. Input snapshots retain the actual values and owners
before expansion consumes them. Tests cover mixed/nested types, nominal quantum
records, zero-width owners, original imports, split/join axis order, honest
Observe effects, dishonest pure labels, closed-only execution and export refusal.
Ordinary results may use small quantum temporaries under the same all-history
gate. New cases use at most three physical bits.

Rust 1.99.1 and MSRV 1.85.0 each pass eight new integration tests, eleven native
tests, ten type tests and twenty-two existing integration tests, with no skips.
The stable combined first regression command still fails on the separately
recorded CLI usage error; its two existing test binaries pass, and the repaired
new binary subsequently passes all eight cases. Warnings-denied all-target
Clippy and the changed inventory/coverage/CI policy checks pass. Maximum
observed child memory is 1,830,436,864 bytes (about 1.70 GiB).

This slice changes no Lean source and uses the prior bound native executable.
Generic/static transport, full qmatch, nominal coherent-table consumers, complete
proof replay/current-record maintenance and hosted CI/review remain unfinished.
The stale current-proof identity check remains a failure, separately from the
successful protected-record continuity check. No new guarantee or preservation
theorem is claimed; #64 and #195 remain open.
